candidate.scope: Quebec-wide generalized polygons and lot numbers from the renovated cadastre registry; not a Montreal-specific layer.
candidate.keyAssessment: Quebec's official cadastre guidance says a lot number identifies each property, so NO_LOT is the meaningful public key. However, the layer's NO_LOT index is non-unique and the feed includes complementary-plan numbers; global uniqueness and a gateway-safe key are not proven. Do not substitute OBJECTID or GlobalID as user-facing parcel IDs.
candidate.sourceSemantics: Officially described as an extract from the MRNF cadastre database, refreshed every two months. A polygon may be a lot or complementary plan; it is indicative only, not a legal boundary. The service warns coordinates have no legal value and directs users to Infolot / a bornage plan for authoritative limits.
candidate.terms: Item credits © Gouvernement du Québec but provides no explicit open-data license. Données Québec FAQ says the Infolot cadastral register is not currently available as open data. Public queryability is not a grant to reproduce or persist geometries; obtain written reuse permission or a specific applicable license before integration.

boundedProbe.additionalValidation: A no-geometry page of 5 returned 5 non-null distinct NO_LOT values (including PC-15368 and PC-12972). returnDistinctValues across all 26 and resultOffset=5 page requests timed out; completeness, offset pagination and uniqueness across the bbox remain unverified. A 3-feature geometry request also timed out.

candidate.integrationRecommendation: Do not add as a general reusable source yet. The live endpoint and native NO_LOT lookup work, but geometry reuse rights are unclear and globally unique stable IDs are not established. If permission is obtained, use a bounded adapter with count/ID caps and verify uniqueness or a documented stable composite key first.

description: Current Quebec cadastre integration assessment, including unsuccessful paging attempts; Montreal runtime remains disabled.
